purpose: Leuprolide is used to treat prostate cancer in men, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and early puberty in children. It works by lowering certain hormone levels in the body. It can help shrink tumors, reduce pain, or slow down early puberty.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes hormones called testosterone and estrogen that can fuel certain conditions like prostate cancer or endometriosis. Leuprolide signals your brain to eventually stop producing these hormones, essentially putting them at very low levels. Think of it like turning down a dial on hormones that are causing problems in your body.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes or sweating, decreased sex drive, mood changes or depression, tiredness, headaches, injection site redness or soreness, weight gain, and bone or joint pain. In men, it may cause breast tenderness or erectile problems. In women, it may cause vaginal dryness or irregular periods.
warnings: Long-term use can weaken your bones, so your doctor may recommend calcium and vitamin D. It can affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have heart problems. In the first few weeks, hormone levels may temporarily rise before they fall, which can briefly worsen symptoms. It should not be used during pregnancy as it can harm the baby. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: Leuprolide is given as an injection — either under the skin or into a muscle — by a healthcare provider. Depending on the formulation, it may be given daily, monthly, every 3 months, every 4 months, or every 6 months. Your doctor will choose the right dose and schedule based on your condition. You do not take this medication as a pill at home.
